### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **131** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/README.md`, `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/index.ts`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**33** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e883c71f8f73db527096ac6cd688d08ba9008338`.

⛔ **14** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/README.md`, `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/index.ts`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `created_at (literal, 43 pages)`
- **60** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **174** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e883c71f8f73db527096ac6cd688d08ba9008338` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3a25ae4a044e7db9276ec2a56b527b5e3709f06d` — the merge of head `7ad755fd0354bec8f8d545b01f7588c15491309e` into base `e883c71f8f73db527096ac6cd688d08ba9008338`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3a25ae4a044e7db9276ec2a56b527b5e3709f06d && git checkout 3a25ae4a044e7db9276ec2a56b527b5e3709f06d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e883c71f8f73db527096ac6cd688d08ba9008338 7ad755fd0354bec8f8d545b01f7588c15491309e && git checkout -B drift-repro e883c71f8f73db527096ac6cd688d08ba9008338 && git merge --no-ff 7ad755fd0354bec8f8d545b01f7588c15491309e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e883c71f8f73db527096ac6cd688d08ba9008338
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e883c71f8f73db527096ac6cd688d08ba9008338` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `57cbdffe2cedda664ee1ea52fe5735a232640ce0`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/audit-checkpoint.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/crypto-provider.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/sealer.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/signer.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/canonical.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/seed.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/jcs.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/index.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-signing-key-audit.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/objects/sys-audit-log.object.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/system/sys-secret.object.ts

Read: card #31908 with every comment, PR #32348 body and net diff against `main` (merge base `7575116c`, 54 files, +2553/-127), ADR-0154 and ADR-0057 on `main`, report 6779152268, and the check-runs on this head. Nothing was built or run. The rest of the diff (tests, census and strictness counts, translations, changeset prose, docs prose) is the lane seat's at TIER_DEFAULT.

Check-runs on this head when read: 65 total, 27 success, 10 skipped, 28 in progress, 0 failed. Still running: Build Core, Test Core 1 to 8 of 8, Test UI 1 to 16 of 16, Type Check UI, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · workspace. Green so far include Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Spec property liveness, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, and Type Check · source gates. The gate verdicts are not complete, so this record does not stand in for them.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`Clause-②: yes (widening)`: right.** `LifecycleSchema` is strict, so `lifecycle.seal` was an unknown-key refusal on `main` and is now accepted (object.zod.ts 1053-1068). The four lifecycle refusals sit under `if (lc.seal)` (1157-1172) and the object-level one returns early with no seal (2998-3021, called at 4506). No object in the tree declares `seal`, so nothing `main` accepts is refused.
- **`Metadata-protocol: added`: right.** One authorable key, `data/Lifecycle:seal`, strict, with a required `valueFields: string[]`. The shape matches ADR-0154 D10 and the names table.
- **`Skills-docs: follow-up owed — skills/objectstack-data/rules/lifecycle.md`: right in form and fact.** The file exists and has no word on `seal`. The seat files the card and rewrites the line to its number before ACCEPT.
- **New spec exports: none.** `refuseUndeclaredSealValueFields` is module-private. The two contract files change jsdoc only.
  - `AuditCheckpointSinkEntry.body` now lists 17 checkpoint members and the amendment members, and they match `CheckpointSignedBody`, `RedactionAmendmentBody` and `ExpiryAmendmentBody` in signed-body.ts 54-119 one for one. Right.
  - The `audit_seal` text in crypto-provider.ts (118-122, 250-258) says the seed handle is inside a signed body and the private handle is in the unsigned `sys_audit_signing_key.private_handle`. That agrees with signer.ts 149-151: a missing handle row signs nothing. Right.
- **Accept-set, wrong in one place (S5):** `ttl.onlyWhen` beside `seal` parses. The schema's own comment at 1154-1156 says each refused policy "would delete part of a sealed window", and a filtered ttl does exactly that.
- **Plugin surface: right.** `AuditPluginOptions.cryptoProvider` is one new optional member (audit-plugin.ts 130-140). The plugin root exports are unchanged; the sealer and signer stay internal (audit-seal/index.ts 6-8).
  - `checkpointSeedContext` and `signingKeyContext` are root exports the CLI reads, and they now throw `SecretCoordinateBoundError` past 128 characters (seed.ts 100-108, 138-149). This is ruled (Q6 (a)), and no stored row can carry such a coordinate.
- **`audit_signing_key_change` joins the action enum with its writer in the same change** (sys-audit-log.object.ts 485, audit-signing-key-audit.ts). Right, as ADR D6 and Q4 (a) say.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/spec` minor: right. One new authorable key; the card's claim names this level.
- `@objectstack/plugin-audit` minor: right. A new option and a new background worker that writes nothing until an object opts in.
- `@objectstack/platform-objects` patch: right. Source comments only.
- The three lines are true as written. The changeset carries the `Clause-②` and `Metadata-protocol` lines with the same values as the PR body. `Check Changeset` is green on this head.
- The changeset says `sys_audit_log`'s own seal comes "in a later release". So a release between slices is expected, which is what makes S5 and S8 matter now.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Pin edits under amendment 6777658851: all four are in the diff and sound.**
  - `sys-audit-log-action-labels.test.ts`: the value is appended last, no value moved.
  - `sys-audit-log-retired-actions.test.ts`: the row names `audit-signing-key-audit.ts` and `LocalCheckpointSigner.createKey`, which is the real call site (signer.ts 174).
  - `metadata-form-zod-reconciliation.test.ts`: one `omit` row, type `object`, path `lifecycle`, key `seal`, with the ruled reason and the P2 revisit.
  - `object-lifecycle-panel-echo-decisions.test.ts`: a one-entry `LIFECYCLE_FORM_OMITTED_KEYS`, pinning seven schema keys and six offered.
- **The empty-chain guard removed in `d12538f2`: the dev is right.** `readWindow` creates a chain at sealer.ts 479-482 and pushes its first leaf at 483-484 in the same iteration. If `leafInput` throws between the two, the exception leaves `readWindow` and the map is discarded. So every chain that reaches `writeChains` holds at least one leaf. `checkpointBodyFromRow` also refuses `leaf_count` 0 (signed-body.ts 250).
- **Dev deviation, the PR body's "a sealed object declares `id` and `created_at` itself":** the tree is narrower than the sentence. `sealedColumnSet` (canonical.ts 150-153) only requires both in the registry's field map. Accepted as a body inaccuracy; the seat corrects the body.
- **Out-of-scope finding, host wiring: escalate to the seat (S9).** No shipped host passes `cryptoProvider`, and no slice owns it. It needs a slice before P4.
- **Out-of-scope finding, no rotation verb:** stands as ruled (Q4). M1 makes it sharper, since nothing can replace a key whose private half is gone.
- **Out-of-scope finding, `sys_secret`'s description string still says three producers:** agreed, it needs a translation regeneration. Nit; a later slice.
- **Out-of-scope finding, the README intro still says "three things":** lane seat.
- **Out-of-scope finding, `dispatch-gates --commands` derives no package suite:** a tooling finding for the seat to file. Test Core is still running on this head.
- **Out-of-scope finding, the closing keyword in #32266's body:** this PR says `Part of #31908` and avoids the spelling; nothing to do here.
- **`open_questions`:** report 6779152268 carries none.
- **New flag, outside the diff (S7):** `sys_audit_checkpoint.row_ids` is a `Field.textarea`, which driver-sql creates with `table.text` (sql-driver-column-creation.ts 815-816). The sealer puts every row id of a chain's hour into it with no cap.

### ④ Design judgment

What holds against ADR-0154:
- **D1, D2, D4.** Leaves are ordered by canonical `created_at` then id (sealer.ts 535). The Merkle root, the previous digest over the JCS body, the column set, the canon version, the seed handle, the fencing token and the key id are all under an Ed25519 signature (545-563). The seed is 32 random bytes, sealed under `[organization or null, sequence]`, and never leaves the process.
- **D3.** Late rows are sealed before windows (351, then 359-367). An empty window writes nothing. The settle lag is applied at 348. A stopped pass resumes its window through the `resumed` set (363-364, 389, 400). A crash between the seed write and the checkpoint leaves only an orphan secret.
- **D5.** A chain is keyed by the row's own `tenant_id`, and the seed context carries the same organization, so one organization's rows cannot enter another's chain.
- **D6.** `sys_audit_signing_key` holds a fingerprint, the public half and a handle id, never key material. The ledger row is written before the key row (signer.ts 174-175) and holds fingerprints only. Trust goes through the wrapped half (149-160).
- **D10.** The key is declared and enforced: `plans()` reads it on every pass (sealer.ts 213-241), and a deployment that cannot seal says so at `error`.
- **S1 loop.** A signature whose key id differs from its bytes is never stored (519-531).

**M1, must-fix. An insert that rejects is treated as a row that was not stored, and the only copy of a referenced secret is deleted.**
- Where: sealer.ts 543-573 and signer.ts 173-185. Both catch a rejected `engine.insert` and call `dropAuditSealSecret`.
- Why the premise is false: the engine rejects an insert after the row is durable. `triggerHooks` rethrows whatever an `afterInsert` handler throws (engine-hooks-and-functions.ts 410-414), and it is called after the driver write (engine-insert.ts 1572). No unit of work is open unless a metadata-bound aborting hook exists (`opensAfterAbortUnit`, same file, 466-479). A lost acknowledgment from a remote driver gives the same result.
- Sealer consequence: a stored, signed checkpoint names a `seed_handle` whose row is gone. The next pass reads that window as sealed and never re-seals it. Its commitments can never be recomputed, so P2 will report an honest window as failed for as long as the rows are kept. ADR D2 requires the seed to stay.
- Signer consequence: an `active` key row names a missing private half. `activeKey()` returns it on every call, `openPrivateHalf` throws at 151, and `createKey` is reached only when there is no active key (190). Sealing stops for the whole deployment, with no recovery path in code. ADR D6 requires the wrapped half to be kept as long as the key row is.
- This is the "deleted key still referenced" case. The other half is safe: a key that failed creation has signed nothing.
- Fix shape: drop the secret only for failures before the insert is attempted (sign failure, lapsed lease). After a rejected insert, re-read the holder by its coordinate and keep the secret when the row exists; otherwise leave the orphan to `os secret orphans`, as the comment at signer.ts 75 already says. Pin both sites with an insert that stores and then rejects.

Should-fix:
- **S1. A window can be sealed twice in one chain.** The pass decides which windows and chains are unsealed at its start (336-351), but reads each chain's head lazily at write time (492-505, 536). A second sealer that reads the head after the first one's insert takes the next free sequence and seals the same rows again; the unique index refuses only an equal sequence. ADR D3's "only if the chain's head is still the one the sealer read" is therefore held trivially.
  - Reachable with a cluster lock when an insert outlives the lease after the `isHeld` check at 564. Routine with the in-process lock on two replicas, since both loops fire at the same instant (190).
  - The info line at 253-257 and ruling Q2 (a) both lean on the index for this. Either refuse a `window` checkpoint when the head already covers that window, or read the heads with the pass-start reads.
  - A double seal also makes the late recount mismatch for seven days, so every pass re-reads those windows.
- **S2. Offset paging can skip rows while the Archiver deletes from the hot store.** `readWindow` pages by `offset` (463-470). A hot delete of earlier rows of the same window between two pages shifts later rows under the offset, and the archive holds only the moved ones. The late recount repairs this inside seven days; in a backlog older than the horizon (what Q3 (a) is for) the skipped rows are never sealed, and P2 would report them unsealed on an honest deployment. Use keyset paging on `(created_at, id)`, as mail-log-body-migration.ts 328 does by id.
- **S3. The chain is read off `tenant_id` only (150).** The platform's tenant column on ordinary objects is `organization_id` (objectql registry.ts 1300). An audit-class object that declares `seal` without a `tenant_id` field gets every organization's rows in the deployment chain, and nothing reports it. The docs promise one checkpoint per organization. Refuse such an object in `plans()` with the once-at-error report, or read the object's tenant column. This is also a carrier note for cloud's `sys_ai_audit_log`.
- **S4. One row or one chain stops every organization's sealing of that object, and it is said once.** Any refusal makes the object's pass throw, so no later chain and no later window is sealed. Examples: a canonical-form refusal (canonical.ts 203-224, 256-263, 284), the Q6 bound, or a malformed head row. `reportOnce` (206-210) then stays silent for the life of the process. A value one organization writes can thus halt sealing for all.
  - Two rules make this reachable on a later opt-in: `time` passes through as text, though dialects spell it differently; and the json rule parses every string, so a top-level JSON string scalar fails or changes type where the driver hands the column back parsed.
  - At least repeat the report while an object is stalled; rule on per-chain isolation before P4.
- **S5. Accept-set gaps in object.zod.ts.**
  - `ttl.onlyWhen` beside `seal` is accepted (1157-1172). Refuse it now: a later refusal is a narrowing. ADR D8 says D10 refuses every other policy. If the seat reads D10's three as closed, it should say so on the card.
  - `valueFields` naming `id` or `created_at` is accepted at authoring and refused only at run time (canonical.ts 150-153). The object refinement already sees the field map and could refuse it there. Ruling Q5 (a) covers the no-rule column types, not these two.
- **S6. The late recount is wider and weaker than stated.** The early return at 392 compares one total over the whole horizon and every organization. So a delete in any window masks a late row in any other; the PR body says "in the same window". ADR D3 re-counts the sealed windows; drop the aggregate shortcut or state it. The loop at 395-402 also runs up to 168 counts without renewing the 60-second lease.
- **S7. `row_ids` on MySQL.** See ③. A `text` column there holds 64 KB, about 1,600 UUIDs, and a longer list fails the insert on every pass, which stalls the object (S4). Fix the column type or bound a checkpoint's size before P4 opts `sys_audit_log` in. The object file is outside this diff, so this is the seat's to place.
- **S8. The key is authorable before expiry exists.** Until P4 the sweeper still deletes sealed rows row by row, with no amendment. An object that opts in between releases will later read as `missing`. The `seal` description (1062-1067) and `objects.mdx` teach the key with an `archive.keep` example and do not say this. Say it in the description, or hold the docs section until P4.
- **S9. Host wiring has no slice.** With no host passing `cryptoProvider`, the fix the error line names (268-272) cannot be applied on any shipped host. P3's refusal to rewrite and P4's default both depend on it.

Nits:
- A failed key-row insert leaves an `audit_signing_key_change` row naming a key that never existed (signer.ts 174-184); a retry writes a second one.
- The in-process lock and its fencing counter are module-level (sealer.ts 153-154), shared by every kernel in a process.
- A non-string `tenant_id` reads as the deployment chain (150).
- `reported` is never cleared, so a fault that returns after a fix is not reported again.
- Duplicate names in `valueFields` parse, and the sealer de-duplicates them (canonical.ts 154).
- After a successful insert, `deliver` runs inside the same `try` (568); it swallows its own errors today, but the structure invites M1 again.

Probes that held: an empty window; a pass stopped mid-window; a signer answering another key id; a planted key row (fails loudly, signs nothing); a row present in both stores (read once, 461-475); clock skew inside the settle lag, and beyond it within seven days (sealed as `late`).

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-8ykewa`
Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzi1tLRTEYwYGtbNCyk`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `041fc793f0304e2f3aeaf9c6a01e6bcc35720265`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/audit-checkpoint.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/crypto-provider.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/sealer.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/signer.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/seal-store.testkit.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/audit-seal-sealer.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/audit-seal-signer.test.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object-lifecycle-seal.test.ts, .changeset/31908-audit-seal-sealer-signer.md, content/docs/data-modeling/objects.mdx, content/docs/references/data/object.mdx

Delta review of `57cbdffe..041fc793`: one fast-forward commit, 10 files, +230/-48, no main merge. Everything outside this delta stands as judged in record 6779418107. Read: that record, the carry comment 6779459920, os-dev-report 6781163584, the PR body, the delta, and the head's sealer.ts, signer.ts, seed.ts and object.zod.ts in full where the delta touches them. Nothing was built or run.

**Check-runs on this head: 0.** There are no check-runs, workflow runs or statuses; five check-suites sit queued and empty. The PR does not merge cleanly: `git merge-tree origin/main 041fc793` conflicts in `content/docs/permissions/tenant-audit-census.mdx` and `docs/audits/2026-08-tenant-audit-write-call-sites.counts.md`, both changed by main's `1f3e6fdb` (#32268). No gate verdict exists for this head, and this record does not stand in for one.

### ① Derived judgments

- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is still right. The two new refusals sit under `if (lc.seal)` (object.zod.ts 1168-1170) and inside `refuseUndeclaredSealValueFields`, which returns early when there is no seal (3004-3013). They narrow only against this PR's earlier, unreleased head. Against main, where `seal` is an unknown-key refusal, the change stays a pure widening. The changeset (line 9) and the PR body carry the same value, and the changeset prose names both refusals.
- `Metadata-protocol: added` is unchanged and right: the delta adds no new key and no new export.
- S5 is fixed. `ttl.onlyWhen` beside `seal` is refused at `['lifecycle','ttl','onlyWhen']`, and `id` or `created_at` in `valueFields` is refused at its index. Both are pinned by path (object-lifecycle-seal.test.ts 123-134). The messages are true: leaves are ordered by `created_at` then `id` (sealer.ts 551).
- S8 is fixed and true. The sentence is in the `seal` description (object.zod.ts 1064-1070), in objects.mdx (244-245), in both generated tables in references/data/object.mdx, and in the changeset. No lifecycle sweeper reads `seal`.
- The other description changes are true: "Reports that at error" matches `report` (sealer.ts 212-217), and the objects.mdx sentence on `id`, `created_at` and `tenant_id` matches `plans()` (229-236). The body's id/created_at sentence is corrected.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` minor, `@objectstack/plugin-audit` minor and `@objectstack/platform-objects` patch are unchanged and still right. The changeset's new prose is true to the tree: the two refusals, the `tenant_id` requirement, the repeated report and the expiry sentence.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev deviation, S1 "at or after": accepted; see ④.
- Dev statement that no main file is in this PR's list: false in the tree. The two census files conflict (above). The dev merges main with `scripts/pm/os-regen-merge.sh` and regenerates the census. The new head needs its own gates. This is not a contract finding, but it blocks ACCEPT.
- Carried and not judged this round, as ordered: S7, S9 and per-chain isolation (6779459920).
- Changed assertions follow from the fixes: the resume test expects 4 `sys_secret` rows (the orphan M1 leaves), and the store double reads `$and`, `$or` and `$gt`. driver-sql compiles `$and` and `$or` (sql-driver-filter-helpers.ts 700-720) and canonicalises datetime comparands (`coerceFilterValue`, 177-220). driver-memory reads both (memory-driver.ts 1644).

### ④ Design judgment

**M1 is fixed at both sites.**
- In the sealer (sealer.ts 559-612), the seed is dropped only in the first `try`, which ends before the insert (587-592). After a rejected insert, the row is re-read by `(sealed_object, chain_key, sequence)`. If it was stored with this seed, it stands with a warning; otherwise the seal rethrows and the seed stays.
- In the signer (signer.ts 173-192), a failed ledger write drops the half, because no key row was attempted. A rejected key-row insert re-reads by fingerprint and keeps the half.
- A re-read that itself fails is caught (600, 190) and treated as not stored.
- A row that lands after the re-read is found by the next pass.
- An orphan at a reused coordinate does not block the retry, because `sys_secret`'s `(namespace, key)` index is not unique (sys-secret.object.ts 173).
- Both sites are pinned with an insert that stores and then rejects.

**S1 is fixed for window checkpoints.**
